title: Sift formal threat model and data-flow boundary map
scope: Desktop research assistant using researcher-supplied model and data-service credentials on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
security_objectives: Raw observations remain local unless the researcher explicitly attaches content to a provider request.
Model-origin actions cannot bypass deterministic policy, sanitization, approval, sandbox, or export controls.
Credentials are stored in the OS credential service and are not placed in model prompts, execution environments, or error messages.
Every released analytical fact is disclosure-controlled, attributable, and tamper-evident.
A failure in parsing, policy loading, provenance validation, or cryptographic verification fails closed.
non_claims: Sift does not claim that pattern matching proves HIPAA de-identification or eliminates re-identification risk.
A hash chain is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof against an attacker who can rewrite all local state.
Best-effort overwrite cannot guarantee erasure from SSD wear-levelled blocks, snapshots, or backups.
Prompt injection cannot be eliminated by text filtering; deterministic tool and output boundaries limit impact.
Sift's own testing is not an independent third-party penetration test.

actors.trust: authorized human controlling the desktop session
external or local model endpoint; output is untrusted
database/cloud/research service; metadata and driver errors are untrusted
may be benign or malicious; all file content and metadata are untrusted
may read stolen storage or influence researcher-writable files
may target dependencies, build inputs, or distributed artifacts

boundaries.destination: another live session runner and UI
controls: runner keyed by resolved session path

boundaries.source: sanitized local stores and researcher action

boundaries.destination: portable encrypted bundle and restore target
all provider, integration, disclosure, and export gates
controls: fixed OS paths or ownership validation

threats.scenario: Raw records or identifiers reach a remote model.
threats.mitigation: schema-only defaults, explicit attachment staging, disclosure review, sanitizer and release policy
threats.residual_risk: A researcher can intentionally paste confidential content; pattern detection is advisory.

threats.scenario: Instructions embedded in names, labels, database metadata, documents, images, or model output attempt to change policy.
threats.mitigation: text normalization plus deterministic tool/policy/approval boundaries
threats.residual_risk: Semantic injection can influence prose; it cannot authorize disallowed execution or disclosure.

threats.scenario: A malicious file uses traversal, symlinks, malformed containers, or output collisions.
threats.mitigation: resolved-path containment, no-follow writes, type/signature checks, safe extraction

threats.scenario: A parser bomb or analysis process exhausts time, RAM, process count, disk, or output.
threats.mitigation: bounded parsing/materialization and parent-enforced execution limits

threats.scenario: Code, driver errors, transport errors, or prompts expose API/database credentials.
threats.mitigation: OS credential storage, execution environment allowlist, transport header injection, layered redaction

threats.scenario: Model-generated code reads outside the project, reaches the network, or spawns surviving children.
threats.mitigation: OS-specific fail-closed sandbox and whole-process-tree termination
threats.residual_risk: Platform sandbox correctness requires ongoing OS-specific qualification.

threats.scenario: Queued turns, attachments, results, or provider history are routed to the wrong project.
threats.mitigation: resolved-path runner identity, session-bound queues, stores, locks, and event filtering

threats.scenario: A released claim cannot be tied to code, data, method, or approval state.
threats.mitigation: hash-chained audit, immutable correction links, exact provenance, optional export signature

threats.scenario: Researcher-writable or malformed enterprise policy silently disables a restriction.
threats.mitigation: trusted location/ownership check and strict fail-closed parsing

threats.scenario: A vulnerable or substituted dependency compromises confidential processing.
threats.mitigation: lock hashes, SBOM, automated scans, signed build/provenance plan
threats.residual_risk: A clean vulnerability database scan cannot prove absence of unknown vulnerabilities.

threats.scenario: Deleted scripts, runs, or sessions remain recoverable on storage or backups.
threats.mitigation: SQLite secure_delete, best-effort overwrite, encrypted bundles, retention controls
threats.residual_risk: Strong deletion depends on storage encryption, snapshot policy, backup lifecycle, and media sanitization.

threats.scenario: A provenance signing key is copied or misused.
threats.mitigation: private key stored in OS credential service and never placed in export
threats.residual_risk: Software-backed keys do not equal hardware-backed organizational signing; key rotation and revocation are deployment responsibilities.

review_triggers: change to sanitizer, release policy, enterprise policy, or sandbox
